messages:
alex: FYI seeing a weird spike of ALB target deregistrations after last night's GPU pool scale. ~12 targets in eu-west-2 went Unhealthy within a 3m window. ALB logs show healthcheck timeouts then DeregisterTargets.

sylvia_infra: same. pattern aligns with gpupool auto-scale event. seems to start when new nodes finish kubelet join and boot containers. Not constant failures — cluster recovers after ~10m.

matt: dug into node-level logs. tcpdump on node shows ALB TCP probes arrive fine, but the TCP handshake to the pod sometimes never completes — RSTs from node shortly after. suspect NAT port churn on egress path colliding with ephemeral ports used by probe responses.

sophia: interesting. ALB healthcheck is _to_ pod IP:port, so response should go directly back to ALB. Why would egress SNAT affect that? Could be our sidecar/egress chain rewriting replies (service mesh or iptables prerouting) or kube-proxy ipvs rules occasionally pointing probe flows to host proxy and triggering source rewrite.

alex: deploy-bot shows autoscaler: gpupool-front scaled 6 -> 20 at 2026-03-19T23:09:51Z. loads of pod churn + CNI rebinds. That could cause transient conntrack churn.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled gpupool-front 6 -> 20 (reason: scheduled backlog) at 2026-03-19T23:09:51Z

matt: commands i ran to reproduce checks:

```
# on affected node
sudo ss -tn sport = :8080 state established | wc -l
sudo conntrack -L | grep ALB_HEALTH_PORT
sudo conntrack -S > /tmp/conntrack-snap
# tcpdump filter for ALB health checks
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 'host 52.95.0.0/16 and port 8080' -w /tmp/alb-hc.pcap
```

matt: conntrack showed old mappings being garbage-collected while new probes created same tuple => kernel issued RST for what it thought was stale half-connection. conntrack spikes correlated exactly with kube-proxy restart during node join.

sylvia_infra: so hypothesis: scale event triggers kube-proxy/CNI restarts, conntrack GC churn + ephemeral port reuse => intermittent RST/timeouts for ALB probe flows => ALB marks target unhealthy and removes it.

alex: mitigation options?

sophia: short-term: increase ALB healthcheck healthy_threshold and timeout so flaps less likely to deregister. also schedule gradual scaleups (rate limit autoscaler) for that pool to avoid large conntrack churn.

matt: longer-term: pin probe source path by enabling hostPort healthchecks (node target group) for gpupool frontends, or add dedicated ENIs for control plane egress so probe responses aren't touched by SNAT/egress churn. also tune conntrack max and gc thresholds.

oncall: action items
- matt: post tcpdump + conntrack snapshots to the incident thread (/tmp/alb-hc.pcap, conntrack-snap)
- sylvia_infra: raise autoscaler rate limit PR for gpupool
- sophia: draft quick config change to healthcheck thresholds and roll in next 20m

alex: thanks. tagging oncall if this regresses: @oncall please watch ALB_TargetHealth for gpupool-front in eu-west-2 and alert if >5 dereg in 10m :thumbsup:

oncall: acknowledged, will monitor and escalate to SRE if > 10% impact
